# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## I. PLACEMENT GAMES
Games where you place objects, numbers, or marks in cells

### A. Light/Illumination
- **Akari** - Place light bulbs that illuminate rows/columns

### B. Number Placement
- **Sudoku** - Place numbers 1-9 in rows, columns, and blocks
- **Nansuke** - Fill blank cells with numbers from a list
- **Makaro** - Fill cells with numbers based on directional arrows
- **Ripple Effect** - Fill cells with consecutive numbers in rooms
- **Kurotto** - Color cells based on number sums extending from circles

### C. Block/Shape Placement
- **Shikaku** - Divide grid into rectangles containing one number
- **Fillomino** - Fill blocks with numbers matching block size
- **LITS** - Place tetrominoes in regions
- **Evolomino** - Place squares on arrows with progressive sizing
- **Shakashaka** - Place triangles in squares to form rectangles
- **Sashigane** - Divide grid into L-shaped blocks

### D. Snake/Sequence Placement
- **Hebi** - Place numbers 1-5 forming connected snakes
- **Pencils** - Draw lines from pencil tips using length numbers

### E. Cell Coloring/Shading
- **Hitori** - Color cells to eliminate duplicate numbers
- **Kurodoko** - Color cells black based on visibility counts
- **Nurikabe** - Color cells black to form walls around white regions
- **Nurimisaki** - Color cells with promontory constraints
- **Usowan** - Color cells based on neighbor counts (with one wrong number)
- **Sto-stone** - Color cells that "drop" to fill bottom half
- **Tilepaint** - Color tiles based on diagonal line counts
- **Norinori** - Color cells in pairs within regions
- **Nuritwin** - Shade two equal-sized blocks per region
- **Heyawake** - Paint cells with constraints on white cell continuity

### F. Block Identification
- **Chained Block** - Identify black cell blocks in chains
- **Choco Banana** - Paint cells forming rectangles/squares
- **Double Choco** - Divide grid into blocks with matching white/gray pairs

## II. LINE DRAWING GAMES
Games where you draw continuous lines or loops

### A. Single Loop Games
- **Slitherlink** - Connect dots to form a loop
- **Masyu** - Draw loop through circles with turn constraints
- **Dotchi-Loop** - Draw loop through white circles with turn rules
- **Nagareru** - Draw loop following wind directions from arrows
- **Yajilin** - Draw loop avoiding black cells indicated by arrows
- **Moon-or-Sun** - Draw loop alternating between moon/sun cells per room
- **Mid-loop** - Draw loop with black circles as midpoints
- **Suraromu** - Draw loop passing through numbered gates in order

### B. Path/Connection Games
- **Numberlink** - Connect pairs of same numbers with non-crossing lines
- **Hashiwokakero** - Connect islands with bridges (1-2 per pair)

## III. MOVEMENT GAMES
Games where you move objects to new positions

- **Satogaeri** - Move circles to countries based on distance numbers
- **Yosenabe** - Move circles into gray areas with sum constraints

## IV. DIVISION/PARTITIONING GAMES
Games where you divide the grid into regions

- **Five Cells** - Divide grid into blocks of exactly 5 cells
- **Juosan** - Fill cells with — or | marks with territory constraints

---

## Alternative Organization by Primary Mechanic

| **Mechanic** | **Games** |
|---|---|
| **Illumination/Visibility** | Akari, Kurodoko, Kurotto |
| **Number Placement** | Sudoku, Nansuke, Makaro, Ripple Effect |
| **Shape/Block Placement** | Shikaku, Fillomino, LITS, Evolomino, Shakashaka, Sashigane |
| **Coloring/Shading** | Hitori, Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Usowan, Sto-stone, Tilepaint, Norinori, Nuritwin, Heyawake, Choco Banana, Double Choco, Chained Block |
| **Loop Drawing** | Slitherlink, Masyu, Dotchi-Loop, Nagareru, Yajilin, Moon-or-Sun, Mid-loop, Suraromu |
| **Path/Connection** | Numberlink, Hashiwokakero, Hebi, Pencils |
| **Movement** | Satogaeri, Yosenabe |
| **Partitioning** | Five Cells, Juosan, Nurimeizu |
